199: 	private Type ifTypeIsIterableToComponent(Type type, JavacAST ast) {
200: 		this.valTreeMaker = ast.getTreeMaker();

202: 		TreeMaker underlying = this.valTreeMaker.getUnderlyingTreeMaker();
203: 		if (underlying != null) this.valTreeMaker.at(-1);
204: 		if (type == null) return null;
205: 		Types types = Types.instance(ast.getContext());
206: 		Type boundType = ReflectiveAccess.Types_upperBound(types, type);
207: 		Type elemTypeIfArray = types.elemtype(boundType);
208: 		if (elemTypeIfArray != null) return elemTypeIfArray;
209: 
210: 		Type iterableType = this.valSymbols.iterableType;
211: 		Type base = types.asSuper(boundType, iterableType.tsym);
212: 		if (base == null) return this.valSymbols.objectType;
213: 
214: 		List<Type> iterableParams = base.allparams();
215: 		if (iterableParams.isEmpty()) return this.valSymbols.objectType;
216: 		Type component = null;
217: 		for (Type iterableParam : iterableParams) {
218: 			component = iterableParam;
219: 			break;
220: 		}
221: 		List<Type> typeArgs = base.getTypeArguments();
222: 		if (typeArgs != null && !typeArgs.isEmpty()) {
223: 			for (Type typeArg : typeArgs) {
224: 				component = typeArg;
225: 				break;
226: 			}
227: 		}
228: 		if (component == null) return this.valSymbols.objectType;
229: 		return ReflectiveAccess.Types_upperBound(types, component);
230: 	}

232: 	private static class ReflectiveAccess {
233: 		private static Method UPPER_BOUND;
234: 		private static Throwable initError;
235: 
236: 		static {
237: 			Method upperBound = null;
238: 			try {
239: 				upperBound = Permit.getMethod(Types.class, "upperBound", Type.class);
240: 			} catch (Throwable e) {
241: 				initError = e;
242: 			}
243: 
244: 			if (upperBound == null) try {
245: 				upperBound = Permit.getMethod(Types.class, "wildUpperBound", Type.class);
246: 			} catch (Throwable e) {
247: 				initError = e;
248: 			}
249: 
250: 			UPPER_BOUND = upperBound;
251: 		}

253: 		public static Type Types_upperBound(Types types, Type type) {
254: 			return (Type) Permit.invokeSneaky(initError, UPPER_BOUND, types, type);

66469e04 [var] various upgrades to var: * var is promoted to the main package. * It is no longer an opt-in thing. * bug: var (unlike val) is allowed in old-style for loops, but if you multi-init: for (var i = 0, j="Foo";;), you now get an error that you can't do that. * tests both for the multi-for situation and the new main package variant.

Log. *facepalm*). We didn’t update log when resolving for i.e. ‘val’, so the caches get all jumbled up. Fixed by setting the Log’s ‘useSource’ method.
b63dd315 Some refinement on var
69eeb9ed a initialization of variable  like "var o = null;" will throw the compile time error "variable initializer is 'null'"
67371e58 imports expanded, idents aligned
710a0460 The  @var annotation has been moved to the experimental package. Added a test of a @var variable with null initialization.
55619e80 added supporting of @var variables. The @var annotation has the same functionality as the @val except 'final' modifier.
9d8c4e40 New feature: FieldDefaults can now be configured to apply to _every_ file, regardless of annotations.
a6170f52 updated some copyright headers and reverted a change to use a TreeMap to force a more deterministic order to file processing in order to aid debugging. Also updated changelog.
6a91c013 [i694] When we resolve anything with inner classes, supertype references in those inner classes that also have val will break, depending on compile order. This should fix it.
7f85149f bugfix: our new trick to try and disable target typing by making the LHS of a 'val' statement be of an unknown type instead of j.l.Object works for Javac8, but breaks Javac6! We now detect this and pick the right strategy based on whether or not the compiler supports target typing.
d330649b more work on JDK8 support: val on generified lub types now works a little better.
5767628e [configuration] Moved ALL ConfigurationKey constants into 'ConfigurationKeys'; that bug where fields in annotation defs causes issues is too endemic to try and work around these.
e24ebbbf [configuration] implementation of flagUsage for all handlers.
08381773 Fix for Issue #591: v1.12.2 doesn't well with netbeans.
7ada401b If val errors out, now at least you see where it happened.
0dbc68a5 Added an optimization to javac: Don't force new resolution rounds if none of the handlers in the next priority level need it.
1be7da76 * Added priorities to handlers, along with implementation of the priority system for javac and ecj. * @Value now makes the class itself final by default.
c900526e Philipp Eichhorn's patch to use marker annotations instead of boolean-returning interface methods for eclipse's postdiet and javac's isResolutionBased.
df5324e2 'val' is no longer legal in basic for loops now. Fixes issue #346

Implemented the javac `@val` recovery fix in `src/core/lombok/javac/handlers/HandleVal.java`.

When the initial attribution of an unqualified generic method call is erroneous, Lombok now temporarily clears the initializer’s cached type while re-attributing the copied AST. This lets javac infer the generic return type instead of retaining the stale `Type cannot be resolved` error. The original initializer type is restored immediately afterward so subsequent compiler processing is unaffected.

- `ant dist` passed.
